summary: Instagram Reels in Hindi are doing nearly all the work: the best videos get 1,300+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 25 views. Videos about sensors in everyday places or robots (PIR motion sensor, robot IR sensor, street light) get the most views, shares and saves. Overall numbers are still small, and the smoke alarm, lift, tap and phone-orientation videos barely get shares or saves.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about one familiar sensor that seems to act like magic (motion, robot, street light). The title opens with a surprising claim or a 'kaise' question, such as 'Aapko Dekhta Nahi!' or 'Robot Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai?', names the sensor, and ends with the 🤔 emoji. The best ones tie the sensor to a robot or a daily-life scene viewers recognise. Shares and saves come from videos that feel like 'now I get it'.
doMore: Open with a bold, slightly shocking claim about a sensor, like 'X Aapko Dekhta Nahi!', then explain it
Pick robot and maker-project angles (IR, PIR, line follower, obstacle avoidance) since they earn the most shares and saves
Post Instagram-first and test a short re-edit for YouTube with a stronger first-second hook
End each video with a save-worthy takeaway, like a one-line wiring tip or a 'save this for your project' prompt
Make follow-up videos on the winners, e.g. PIR part 2 or IR sensor in a robot, and keep using the same title format
stopDoing: Posting near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector and two IR sensor videos) that split the audience
Mixing in English videos or flat, generic titles like 'Smoke Detector Fire Kaise Sense Karta Hai?' with no surprise
